integrity of the mechanical seal support system

facts.title: potential incident - thermal exposure at P-7113

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 2 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control HYDROCARBON_TRANSFER_CONTROL: the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels had been bypassed, and the ICAM investigation classified this as an organisational factor.
Control SEAL_SUPPORT_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY: the integrity of the mechanical seal support system was never verified as effective, and the ICAM investigation classified this as an organisational factor.

recommendations: Confirm at the next critical control verification that the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels on P-7113 performs as designed.
response.sequence: Work was under way in managing hydrocarbon transfer and storage, specifically transferring hydrocarbon between vessels. P-7113 (export transfer pumps) is in service for tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family. The task proceeded during a planned shutdown while the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels had been bypassed. The thermal energy involved is held as hot surface, and the recorded presentation was burn, ignition, scald.
response.summary: On 28 October 2017 a potential incident was recorded on P-7113 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during a planned shutdown; thermal energy held as hot surface was not released.
